values:
The genes encoding the protocatechuate 4,5-dioxygenase of Sphingomonas sp. SYK6 were identified by functional complementation of Pseudomonas putida. A DNA fragment that conferred the ability to grow on vanillate and protocatechuate on Pseudomonas putida was sequenced and found to contain two genes, ligA and ligB, which encode the two subunits of the enzyme [Noda90].

The two genes were initially cloned and overexpressed in Escherichia coli using the lac promoter, but the highly expressed proteins formed inclusion bodies [Noda90]. His tag-fused ligAB genes were expressed under the control of the T7 promoter and produced in large quantities in soluble fom [Kasai07]. The His-tagged protein was purified to near homogeneity by Ni affinity chromatography.

In addition to protocatechuate the enzyme also catalyzes the ring opening of 3-O-methylgallate. This reaction forms two products - 2-pyrone-4,6-dicarboxylate and 5-carboxyvanillate, similar to the reaction catalyzed by the desZ-encoded 3-O-methylgallate 3,4-dioxygenase [Kasai07].

values:
The desZ gene of Sphingomonas sp. SYK6 was discovered by its ability to confer 3-O-methylgallate degradation activity on Escherichia coli.

The enzyme was purified to near homogeneity and characterized. It showed relatively high dioxygenase activity for 3-O-methylgallate (3.5 U/mg) and gallate (1.3 U/mg), and approximately 10 times lower activity for protocatechuate.

Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis identified two products - 2-pyrone-4,6-dicarboxylate and 5-carboxyvanillate, suggesting that the enzyme catalyzes a 3,4-cleavage of the substrate [Kasai04].
